# AM33: view-timeout backoff for consecutive absent leaders (v1.2)

Generated by gov5 from its pacemaker (`hotstuff.Pacemaker.TimeoutDuration`, `SetCommitteeSize`,
`hotstuff.BackoffGroupSize`), `hotstuff.RoundState` (the consecutive-timeout count) and `hotstuff.ViewAfterTimeout`:
`go test -tags nosqlite,noboltdb ./internal -run TestProfile1VectorAM33`
(`N42_PROFILE1_VECTORS_UPDATE=1` rewrites the file; `N42_PROFILE1_VECTORS_MIRROR=<dir>` also writes it to `<dir>/AM33/`).
gov5 commit: a64a7947 (branch feat/p1-vectors-e2; the rule itself: ebc7edb9, the SyncInfo reset removal: 44390bfe).

## Rule (AM33, agreed 2026-11-26)

    timeout(c) = min(base_eff * 2^floor(c / g), max),   g = min(f + 1, 3),   f = floor((n - 1) / 3)

- `c` increments on each local view timeout; it resets on a commit QC (Decide) and on a QC-based view jump, never on a
  TC (gov5 no longer resets it on a TC adopted from SyncInfo).
- A view's timer is `timeout(c)` with `c` as it stands on entering the view.
- `base_eff` is the local adaptive base `max(base, 2 * p95 commit latency)`, capped at max. These vectors have no
  latency samples, so `base_eff = base`.
- n is the size of the validator set the engine holds when it starts the view timer.

## File `timeout_backoff.json`

| Section | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `groups` | n -> f, g for n = 1..7, 10, 100, 512 |
| `timeouts` | timeout(c) for c = 0..12, n = 4, 7, 100, at base 24 s / max 96 s (gate 5d) and at the standard genesis's 6 s / 30 s; `previousRuleMsByC` = g = 1 |
| `runs` | per view: leader, c on entry, its timeout, TC or QC, next view; `gapMs` = sum of the TC views' timeouts; `previousRuleGapMs` = the same run with g = 1 |

Runs: `gate-5d` (n = 100, T = 1, leaders 57..62 absent: 216 s, previously 456 s of timeouts; the 464 s gap measured in
gate 5d adds the block interval); `n{4,7,100}-T1-k{1..6}` and `n100-T1-k33` (k consecutive absent leaders);
`n{4,7,100}-T8-k3` (T = 8, rotate-on-timeout skips each dead window); `am32-n{4,7,100}` (T = 8, E = 50, the leader of
window 96..103 silent from view 98: TC(98) clamps to boundary 101, same leader, then TC(101) -> 104) at 24 s / 96 s and
`-p1` at 6 s / 30 s; `am32-n*-next-dead` (the clamp followed by a second absent leader).

## Interactions

- AM32: the second TC that the epoch clamp lands on the same dead leader is no longer doubled when g >= 2 (n >= 4):
  the clamp case costs 2 * base (48 s at 24 s), not M3a's `base + 2 * base = 72 s`.
- Adaptive base: unchanged; the group divides only the exponent. A node whose p95 commit latency is above base / 2 starts
  from a larger base, so absolute timeouts differ between nodes; the TC sequences do not.
